preconditions.description: t is an integer between 1 and 10^4 inclusive, representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(n == int(n) and 1 <= n <= 10**5 for n in [int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::2]])
preconditions.description: Each test case's n is an integer between 1 and 10^5 inclusive, representing the number of problems.

preconditions.expression: all(len(a) == n and all(1 <= int(x) <= n for x in a) for n, a in zip([int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::2]], [line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[2::2]]))
preconditions.description: For each test case, the tags a are a list of n integers, each between 1 and n inclusive.

postconditions.description: The output is a newline-separated list of results, one per test case.

postconditions.expression: all(result == -1 or (result == int(result) and 0 <= result <= n - 1) for result, n in zip(results, [int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::2]]))
postconditions.description: Each result is either -1 (no valid permutation) or a non-negative integer representing the minimum cost of a valid permutation.

postconditions.expression: all(any(all(a[p[i]] != a[p[i+1]] for i in range(n-1)) for p in permutations(range(1, n+1))) or result == -1 for result, n, a in zip(results, [int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::2]], [line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[2::2]]))
postconditions.description: If a valid permutation exists, the result is the minimum cost (number of non-adjacent consecutive pairs) among all valid permutations; otherwise, the result is -1.

postconditions.expression: all(result == min(sum(1 for i in range(n-1) if abs(p[i+1] - p[i]) > 1) for p in valid_permutations) if any(all(a[p[i]] != a[p[i+1]] for i in range(n-1)) for p in permutations(range(1, n+1))) else result == -1 for result, n, a in zip(results, [int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1::2]], [line.split() for line in stdin.splitlines()[2::2]]))
postconditions.description: The result is the minimum cost of a permutation where no two consecutive problems have the same tag, or -1 if no such permutation exists.
